results.fact: Waypoint list names 'Red Pass' as a mid-route junction, but the route's own prose never goes there
results.correct_value: The scramble leaves the Commonwealth Creek trail at a cairn a few hundred yards before the small pond; Red Pass (about 5,300 ft) lies further up the same trail and is not on this route's ascent line. The 'Red Pass' pin should be dropped from this route's waypoint list (or replaced by a pin for the cairn turnoff), which is a pin-list edit outside a text/number patch.
results.evidence: The WTA route description puts the scramble takeoff at a cairn in the middle of the path before the small pond (reach the pond and you have gone ~300 yards too far), with the trail continuing to Red Pass at 5,300 ft. Mountain Project's East Ridge (Lundin Peak) approach follows the Commonwealth Creek trail up to Red Pass, passing Red Mountain on the right and Red Pond on the left, so Red Pass is beyond the Red Mountain turnoff. The row's approach, climbing_route and itinerary agree. Contradiction confirmed, but the fix is removing/relocating a waypoint pin, which this pass may not do; no patch written.

results.fact: dist_km is one-way while the itinerary/total note give round-trip mileage
results.evidence: dist_km is the ONE-WAY approach figure by catalog convention ('Approach (one way)'); 6.45 km = 4.0 mi, exactly half the itinerary's 8-mile round trip and the approach variant's 12.9 km round trip. WTA also gives 8.0 mi round trip / 2,900 ft, matching the row.

results.fact: Route's own approach names a saddle belonging to a different peak (Lundin/East Lundin) rather than Red Mountain
results.correct_value: This route is the East Ridge of LUNDIN PEAK (6,057 ft), not Red Mountain: from Red Pass a climbers' path goes WEST over Lundin's east and middle false summits to the saddle below Lundin's main summit, where the short 30 m easy-fifth pitch with three big bolts leads to the top. The approach sentence naming the Lundin/East Lundin saddle is correct; what is wrong is the row's filing under Red Mountain (area_id), its high_point_ft 5890 (Red Mountain's summit), and the overview/beta/pro_tips/watch_out/baseFinding framing it as a Red Mountain ridge. Needs re-filing to a Lundin Peak area (area_id is out of scope); after that high_point_ft should become 6057 and the prose should drop the Red Mountain framing.
results.evidence: Mountain Project files 'East Ridge' (Easy 5th, 100 ft, three large bolts, begins at the saddle between Lundin and East Lundin peak, approached PCT -> Commonwealth Creek trail -> Red Pass -> west on a climbers' path) under Lundin Peak, not Red Mountain. Independent trip reports (yellowleaf 2007 'Lundin Peak via east ridge'; mountainwerks 2001 'Lundin Peak East Ridge') describe the same line from Red/Lundin Pass over Lundin's east and middle peaks to the main summit, with big bolts and a rap station on the final east ridge. Patching the prose to say Lundin while the row stays filed on Red Mountain (header shows Red Mountain's elevation) would create a new contradiction, so no patch is written.

results.fact: nature of the finish (one short 5.0 pitch vs. a longer technical finish)
results.correct_value: Above the couloir: third-class ledges and ramps up and right, one short low fifth-class (5.0) pitch, then a short scramble to the Balanced Rock.
results.evidence: Mountain Project's Northeast Couloir (Sherpa Peak) says to scramble up and right from the top of the couloir to the balanced rock, finishing with one short 5.0 pitch. SummitPost's N.E. Couloir page describes 3rd-class ledges and ramps to a single low 5th-class pitch followed by a short scramble to the Balanced Rock. No second source supports the baseFinding's chimney/mid-fifth/tunnel sequence, so that sentence and the matching approach-variant hazard are brought into line with overview/grade/beta.
